title: 还是: A or B?
explain: 还是 means 'or' in a question that asks someone to choose: 你喝红茶还是绿茶？ 'Do you drink black tea or green tea?' Do not add 吗: the question already asks for a choice.
还是 also means 'had better' in a suggestion: 太远了，我们还是打车吧 'It is too far; we had better take a taxi'.
In an ordinary statement 'or' is a different word, so 还是 is for questions and suggestions.

examples.en: Do you drink black tea or green tea?
Are you going today or tomorrow?

examples.zh: 我们坐公交车还是打车？
examples.en: Shall we take the bus or a taxi?

examples.zh: 太远了，我们还是打车吧。
examples.en: It is too far; we had better take a taxi.

mistakes: Do not put 吗 at the end of a 还是 question. 你喝咖啡还是茶吗 is wrong; drop 吗.

q.en: Do you like red or green?
q.explain: Option A + 还是 + option B.

q.zh: 他是你哥哥还是你弟弟？
q.en: Is he your older brother or your younger brother?
q.explain: 还是 sits between the two choices.

q.en: Do you drink coffee or milk tea?
q.explain: 还是 means 'or' in a choice question.

q.en: Are you going or am I going?
q.explain: A 还是 question does not take 吗.

q.zh: 太晚了，我们还是回家吧。
q.en: It is too late; we had better go home.
q.explain: 还是 can also mean 'had better'.

title: 得 and 地: how an action is done
explain: To say how well or how fast someone does something, put 得 after the verb and the description after 得: 他跑得很快 'He runs very fast'; 她写得很好 'She writes very well'. For the negative put 不 before the adjective: 他跑得不快.
If the verb has an object, say the object first: 她汉语说得很好 'She speaks Chinese very well' (or repeat the verb: 她说汉语说得很好).
地 goes before a verb to say how: adjective + 地 + verb. 高兴地说 'say happily'; 弟弟高兴地跑回家 'My younger brother ran home happily'.
The three words 的, 得 and 地 all sound like de. 的 comes before a noun, 地 comes before a verb, and 得 comes after a verb.

examples.en: He runs very fast.
She speaks Chinese very well.
We had a great time yesterday.
My younger brother ran home happily.

mistakes: Do not leave out 得. 他跑很快 is heard in casual speech but is not standard; say 他跑得很快.

q.en: She writes very well.
q.explain: Verb + 得 + 很 + adjective.

q.en: My older brother swims very fast.
q.explain: 游 + 得 + 很快.

q.en: He speaks very slowly.
q.explain: 得 comes after the verb.

q.en: My younger sister laughed happily.
q.explain: 地 comes before the verb.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: She runs very fast?
q.en: She runs very fast.
q.explain: After a verb, use 得, not 地.

title: 每, 经常, 有时 and 什么都
explain: 每 means 'every': 每天 'every day', 每个人 'everyone', 每次 'every time'. After 每 the sentence usually has 都: 每个人都喜欢 'Everyone likes it'; 我每天都喝茶 'I drink tea every day'.
How often: 经常 'often' and 有时 'sometimes' go before the verb: 我经常看电影 'I often watch movies'; 我有时坐地铁，有时打车 'Sometimes I take the subway, sometimes a taxi'.

A question word + 都 means 'everything, everyone, everywhere': 我什么都喜欢吃 'I like eating everything'. With a negative it means 'nothing at all': 我什么都不想吃 'I do not want to eat anything' (here 也 also works: 我什么也不想吃); 谁都 'everyone'; 哪儿都 'everywhere'.

examples.zh: 每天早上我都喝一杯茶。
examples.en: Every morning I drink a cup of tea.
He often goes to the mall.

examples.zh: 我有时坐地铁，有时打车。
examples.en: Sometimes I take the subway, sometimes a taxi.
I like eating everything.

mistakes: After 每 + noun, add 都 before the verb: 每个人都喜欢. After 什么 meaning 'everything' add 都: 我什么都吃. (In a positive sentence 也 does not work there.)

q.en: He takes the subway every day.
q.explain: 每天 + 都 + verb.

q.en: I often watch movies at home.
q.explain: 经常 goes before the verb.

q.en: I do not want to eat anything.
q.explain: 什么 + 都 + 不 means nothing at all.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: Everyone likes this movie?
options: 每个人都喜欢这个电影。
每个人喜欢都这个电影。
q.zh: 每个人都喜欢这个电影。
q.en: Everyone likes this movie.
q.explain: 都 goes before the verb, after 每个人.

q.zh: 我弟弟有时踢足球，不是每天都踢。
q.en: My younger brother sometimes plays soccer, not every day.
q.explain: 有时 means sometimes.

title: Counting: 条, 位, 间, 次, 万 and 多
explain: Every counted noun needs a measure word between the number and the noun. New ones: 条 for long, thin things (一条裤子 'a pair of trousers', 一条鱼 'a fish'); 位 for people, politely (一位老师 'a teacher'); 间 for rooms (一间教室 'a classroom').
To count how many times an action happens, put 次 after the verb and number: 我去过三次中国 'I have been to China three times'; 请再说一次 'Please say it once more'.
万 means ten thousand: 一万 '10,000'. In speech 20,000 is 两万. 多 after a number means 'more than': 二十多个学生 'more than twenty students'.

examples.zh: 我买了一条红色的裤子。
examples.en: I bought a pair of red trousers.
This is a new teacher.
This classroom is big.
I have been to China three times.

mistakes: Do not put the number straight in front of the noun. 一裤子 is wrong; you need a measure word: 一条裤子.

q.en: I have a pair of black trousers.
q.explain: Number + 条 + noun.

q.en: This teacher teaches Chinese.
q.explain: 这 + 位 + noun.

q.en: Please say it once more.
q.explain: 次 counts how many times.

q.en: I bought three fish.
q.explain: 条 goes with long, thin things like fish.

q.prompt: Which is the usual way to say 20,000 in speech?
q.en: This bag is 20,000 yuan.
q.explain: In speech 20,000 is 两万.

title: Result complements: 完, 错 and 懂
explain: A result complement is a short word after the verb that tells the result of the action: 做完 'finish doing', 写错 'write wrongly', 听懂 'understand by listening'. 我吃完饭了 'I have finished eating'.
Put 不 between the verb and the complement to say 'cannot': 听不懂 'cannot understand (by listening)', 看不懂 'cannot understand (by reading)'.
Put 没 before the whole verb + complement for 'did not': 我没听懂 'I did not understand'.

examples.en: I have finished eating.
Did you understand?
He wrote my name wrongly.

examples.zh: 老师说得太快，我听不懂。
examples.en: The teacher speaks too fast; I cannot understand.

mistakes: For 'did not', put 没 before the whole verb + complement: 我没听懂, not 我听没懂.

q.en: I have finished this book.
q.explain: Verb + 完 + object + 了.

q.en: He did not understand what the teacher said.
q.explain: 没 + verb + 懂.

q.zh: 对不起，我写错了你的名字。
q.en: Sorry, I wrote your name wrongly.
q.explain: 错 shows the result was wrong.

q.en: It is too fast; I cannot understand.
q.explain: 听不懂 means cannot understand.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: I did not understand?
q.en: I did not understand.
q.explain: 没 goes before the verb.

title: 来 and 去: coming and going in a direction
explain: Add 来 or 去 after 上, 下, 进, 出, 回 and 过 to show direction. 来 means toward the speaker; 去 means away from the speaker: 他进来了 'He came in' (toward me); 我进去了 'I went in' (away from me).
The pairs are 上来 / 上去 (up), 下来 / 下去 (down), 进来 / 进去 (in), 出来 / 出去 (out), 回来 / 回去 (back) and 过来 / 过去 (over).
With a place, the place goes in between: 他回家去了 'He has gone home'; 她进教室来了 'She came into the classroom'.
起来 is a different use: 快起来 'Get up quickly'; 她笑起来了 'She started laughing'.

examples.en: Please come in and sit down.
He has gone home.
Come down, and we will go together.
She started laughing.

mistakes: Choose 来 or 去 by where the speaker is. Said from inside the room, 'Come in!' is 请进来; said by someone who is walking in, 'I am going in' uses 进去.

q.en: The teacher came into the classroom.
q.explain: Place goes between 进 and 来.

q.en: Come back quickly.
q.explain: 回来 means come back toward the speaker.

q.en: My older brother has already gone back.
q.explain: 回去 means go back, away from the speaker.

q.en: It is cold outside; come in quickly.
q.explain: 进来 means come in toward the speaker.

q.prompt: You are inside the room and want to tell someone at the door to come in. Which sentence?
q.en: Please come in!
q.explain: Inside the room, the person comes toward you: 进来.

title: 跟 and 一起: doing it with someone
explain: 跟 means 'with': 我跟朋友去看电影 'I go to see a movie with a friend'. 一起 means 'together' and goes before the verb: 我们一起去 'We go together'. Often both appear: 我跟朋友一起去旅游.
跟 can also mean 'to' when you talk to someone: 我跟老师说话 'I talk to the teacher'.
To invite someone, add 吧: 我们一起吃饭吧 'Let us eat together'.

examples.en: I go travelling with a friend.
Let us eat together.
Did you tell the teacher?
She often goes to the mall with her mom.

mistakes: Put 跟 + someone before the verb. 我去商场跟妈妈 is wrong; say 我跟妈妈去商场.

q.en: I play soccer with my older brother.
q.explain: 跟 + someone + 一起 + verb.

q.en: They walk to school together.
q.explain: 一起 goes before the verb.

q.en: I want to talk to the teacher.
q.explain: 跟 means with or to.

q.zh: 明天我们一起去看电影吧。
q.en: Let us go and see a movie together tomorrow.
q.explain: 一起 means together.

q.en: I go to the mall with Mom.
q.explain: 跟 + someone goes before the verb.

title: 是…的: how, when or where it happened
explain: Use 是…的 when something already happened and you want to talk about HOW, WHEN, WHERE or WITH WHOM: 我是昨天来的 'I came yesterday' (the point is when). 你是怎么来的？ 'How did you come?' 我是坐地铁来的 'I came by subway'.
是 can be dropped in speech: 我昨天来的. For the negative keep 是 and add 不: 我不是坐地铁来的 'I did not come by subway'.
Compare 了 and 是…的: 我昨天来了 only says that you came; 我是昨天来的 stresses when.

examples.en: I came yesterday.
How did you come?
I came by subway.
He did not come from abroad.

mistakes: Do not use 了 and 的 together in this pattern. 我是昨天来了的 is wrong; say 我是昨天来的.

q.en: I came by taxi.
q.explain: 是 + how + verb + 的.

q.en: When did you arrive?
q.explain: 是 + when + verb + 的.

q.en: It was here that he learned Chinese.
q.explain: 的 closes the 是…的 pattern.

q.en: She came together with her friends.
q.explain: Verb comes before the final 的.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: I did not come by taxi?
q.en: I did not come by taxi.
q.explain: Negate 是…的 with 不是.

title: 可能, 希望 and 准备
explain: 可能 means 'maybe, might': 他可能在家 'He might be at home'; 明天可能下雨 'It may rain tomorrow'. For 'might not' put 不 after 可能: 他可能不来. 不可能 means 'impossible'.
希望 means 'to hope' and is followed by a whole sentence: 我希望明天是晴天 'I hope tomorrow is sunny'; 希望你喜欢 'I hope you like it'.
准备 means 'to get ready' or 'to plan to': 我准备明年出国旅游 'I plan to travel abroad next year'; 我在准备考试 'I am preparing for the exam'.

examples.en: He may not be at home.
It may rain tomorrow.
I hope tomorrow is sunny.
I plan to travel abroad next year.

mistakes: Do not use 不可能 for 'might not'. 不可能 means 'it cannot be'. For 'might not' say 可能不: 他可能不来.

q.en: He might be sleeping.
q.explain: 可能 goes before the verb.

q.en: I plan to go and buy medicine tomorrow.
q.explain: 准备 + verb.

q.zh: 我希望你喜欢这个手表。
q.en: I hope you like this watch.
q.explain: 希望 is followed by a whole sentence.

q.en: It might rain today.
q.explain: 可能 means might.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: He might not come?
q.en: He might not come.
q.explain: 不可能 means impossible; 可能不 means might not.

title: 多 questions, …的时候 and doubled verbs
explain: 多 + adjective asks 'how …?' about size, age, height or distance: 你多大了？ 'How old are you?'; 他有多高？ 'How tall is he?'; 学校离这里有多远？ 'How far is the school from here?' Use the 'big' side of the pair: 多高 (you do not ask how short), 多远 (not 多近).
…的时候 means 'when …': put it after the clause, and put the whole time phrase before the main verb: 吃饭的时候，别看手机 'Do not look at your phone when eating'; 我小的时候，住在中国 'When I was little, I lived in China'.

Doubling a verb makes an action short and light, like 'have a look' or 'take a moment to': 看看, 听听, 想想, 问问, 走走. 你看看这个 'Have a look at this'; 我们出去走走吧 'Let us go out for a walk'. The second syllable is light.

examples.en: How old are you this year?

examples.zh: 下雨的时候，我们在家看电影。
examples.en: When it rains, we watch movies at home.
Think about it some more, okay?
Please ask the teacher.

mistakes: Do not ask with the 'small' word. Ask 多远 (how far), not 多近.

q.en: How far is your home from school?
q.explain: 离 … 有 + 多 + 远.

q.en: How tall is he?
q.explain: 多 + adjective asks how big, tall or far.

q.en: Do not look at your phone when eating.
q.explain: The …的时候 phrase comes before the main clause.

q.prompt: Which sentence asks how far it is?
q.en: How far is the station from here?
q.explain: Ask with the 'big' word: 多远.

q.en: Think about it again.
q.explain: Doubling the verb: 想想.
